chapters.title: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned

shots.text: Meet Ada. Her homework is finished. The answer looks perfectly clear. But close the screen, and something changes.
shots.caption: The page is finished. Is the learning?
shots.purpose: Ada closes a completed answer and hesitates over an empty page.

shots.title: Two things can improve
shots.caption: A better product and a stronger skill are separate goals.
shots.text: An excellent answer is one kind of success. Being able to explain and adapt it yourself is another. They can grow together, but one does not guarantee the other.
shots.purpose: Two things can improve

shots.text: Does artificial intelligence help you learn, or just finish? The difference shows up when the help goes away.
shots.caption: What remains when the help goes away?
shots.purpose: Title opens from the empty answer circle; Ada presents the question.

shots.text: Finishing with help is one test. Doing it alone is another. Remembering later, and solving a different problem, are two more.
shots.caption: Help now. Alone. Later. Somewhere new.
shots.purpose: Four physical medallions expose four different outcome measures.

shots.title: First: performance with help
shots.caption: What can the person and the tool do together?
shots.text: With the tool open, you are measuring a partnership. The result can be impressive. It still leaves open how much of the method belongs to the learner.
shots.purpose: First: performance with help

shots.title: Second: an independent attempt
shots.caption: Close the tool. Keep the question.
shots.text: Remove the assistance and try a fresh problem. Can you choose a first step, explain your choices, and notice when the result makes no sense?
shots.purpose: Second: an independent attempt

shots.title: Third and fourth: later and elsewhere
shots.caption: A familiar page cannot answer every learning question.
shots.text: A later test asks what remains after time passes. A changed situation asks whether you recognize where the method applies. Those questions deserve separate evidence.
shots.purpose: Third and fourth: later and elsewhere

shots.text: In a randomized study of nearly a thousand high school mathematics students in Turkey, an unrestricted chatbot improved practice grades by forty eight percent, compared with the control group.
shots.caption: Practice grades: +48% relative to control.
shots.purpose: A Turkish classroom and a GPT-4 terminal establish the randomized study; the practice result stamps onto paper.

shots.title: Read the comparison carefully
shots.caption: Relative change is not a percentage-point change.
shots.text: That figure is relative to the control group's practice grades. It does not mean forty eight extra percentage points, or the same improvement for every student.
shots.purpose: Read the comparison carefully

shots.text: But on the exam without the tool, that group scored seventeen percent lower. Better homework performance had hidden weaker independent performance.
shots.caption: Unaided exam grades: −17% relative to control.
shots.purpose: The screen is covered. A second test paper reveals the independent-performance reversal.

shots.title: One experiment, two outcomes
shots.caption: Keep the practice result beside the unaided result.
shots.text: Random assignment provides stronger evidence than comparing people who chose a chatbot with those who did not. But the result still belongs to this particular setting.
shots.purpose: One experiment, two outcomes

shots.text: A tutor designed around teacher supplied hints largely removed that penalty. It did not produce a statistically significant exam improvement over the control group.
shots.caption: Teacher-designed hints changed the outcome.
shots.purpose: The answer card becomes a hint card; show mitigation without inventing an exam gain.

shots.title: The guardrails matter
shots.caption: Removing a penalty is different from proving a gain.
shots.text: The guarded tutor used teacher designed hints. Its result does not mean any friendly chatbot will teach well. The design of the help matters.
shots.purpose: The guardrails matter

shots.text: In a separate college physics experiment, a carefully designed tutor led to higher immediate test scores than an active classroom lesson.
shots.caption: Tutor design matters.
shots.purpose: A physics learner tests a pendulum with a structured tutor; establish a separate experiment.

shots.title: Look at the actual teaching task
shots.caption: Different subjects. Different learners. Different tutors.
shots.text: This comparison involved a structured tutor and an active classroom lesson. It compares those teaching arrangements, not all machines with all teachers.
shots.purpose: Look at the actual teaching task

shots.text: These are different designs and different settings. Neither result tells us what every learner will remember months later.
shots.caption: An immediate test is not a long-term test.
shots.purpose: A moving calendar and clock distinguish immediate testing from later memory.

shots.title: Avoid the universal headline
shots.caption: Ask what was taught, compared and measured.
shots.text: Together, these studies suggest asking which designs preserve the learner's thinking. They do not establish one universal percentage for how much artificial intelligence helps or harms learning.
shots.purpose: Avoid the universal headline

shots.title: The answer feels familiar
shots.caption: Following an explanation is one experience.
shots.text: Read a clear explanation twice and its steps can feel obvious. That feeling does not prove you could reconstruct the explanation without looking.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: The answer feels familiar

shots.title: Close the book
shots.caption: Reconstructing it is a different task.
shots.text: When the page disappears, its prompts disappear too. You must select the idea, retrieve the steps, and organize them. A blank sheet can expose hidden gaps.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: Close the book

shots.title: A classic retrieval experiment
shots.caption: Study passages. Practise recall. Test later.
shots.text: In a classic prose passage experiment, repeated study looked better on the immediate test. Earlier recall tests helped more when people were tested after a delay.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: A classic retrieval experiment

shots.title: Confidence did not settle it
shots.caption: A confident prediction is still a prediction.
shots.text: Repeated studying also increased confidence. Yet the delayed advantage favored retrieval practice. Feeling fluent and remembering later were different outcomes in these experiments.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: Confidence did not settle it

shots.title: Retrieve, then check
shots.caption: An attempt gives feedback something to work on.
shots.text: Try recalling before reopening the answer, then check your work. Correct the missing or mistaken parts. An unsuccessful attempt is information, not a reason to keep practising errors.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: Retrieve, then check

shots.title: Spread the attempts
shots.caption: Return after some time has passed.
shots.text: In a mathematics experiment by Rohrer and Taylor, practice spread across sessions produced better performance a week later than practice concentrated in one session.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: Spread the attempts

shots.title: Mix problems that need different methods
shots.caption: Choosing a method is part of the work.
shots.text: Their second experiment favored mixing problem types over blocking them on a later test. Mixing asks you to identify the problem before selecting a procedure.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: Mix problems that need different methods

shots.title: Apply the principle with care
shots.caption: These learning studies were not chatbot trials.
shots.text: These studies support independent practice and later checks. They do not prove that one particular chatbot prompt or practice schedule will work for every person.
shots.chapter: 03 · Why easy can feel like learned
shots.purpose: Apply the principle with care

shots.text: So, when learning is the goal, give the tool a different job. Let it support the thinking you need to practise.
shots.caption: Keep the thinking you need to practise.
shots.purpose: Ada moves the terminal aside to put her own working sheet in the centre.

shots.text: Step one. Make an attempt. If you know enough to start, put your own first step on the page.
shots.caption: Step one. Make an attempt.
shots.purpose: First numbered medallion; Ada writes her own attempt.

shots.text: For a completely new topic, study a clear worked example first. A beginner needs guidance, not a guessing contest.
shots.caption: New topic? Start with a worked example.
shots.purpose: Open example book supports a novice without pretending unassisted struggle is always best.

shots.title: Guidance has a job
shots.caption: Reduce confusion without removing every decision.
shots.text: If the notation is unfamiliar, struggling alone can be unhelpful. A worked example provides a path to inspect. Can the learner explain that path?
shots.purpose: Guidance has a job

shots.title: An equation makes a promise
shots.caption: Both sides name the same quantity.
shots.text: Both sides of Ada's equation are equal. Each operation must preserve that equality. She is keeping the balance true, not moving symbols by magic.
shots.purpose: An equation makes a promise

shots.text: Now ask for a hint about the exact step you cannot explain. Ask it to check your reasoning before showing the whole solution.
shots.caption: Ask for the next useful hint.
shots.purpose: Round detail callout shows the specific hint request and a partial response.

shots.text: Ada needs to solve two times a number, plus three, equals eleven. Her hint is simple: undo the addition first.
shots.caption: Undo the addition first.
shots.purpose: Close-up of the actual algebra and subtraction action.

shots.title: Subtract from both sides
shots.caption: Keep the equality true while simplifying.
shots.text: Subtracting three undoes the addition on the left. Doing the same on the right leaves eight. Two times the unknown must therefore equal eight.
shots.purpose: Subtract from both sides

shots.title: Then divide both sides
shots.caption: Two equal groups share a total of eight.
shots.text: Divide both sides by two. One copy of the unknown equals four. That reasoning still applies when the next equation uses different numbers.
shots.purpose: Then divide both sides

shots.title: A small check before moving on
shots.caption: Pause and explain one step in your own words.
shots.text: Explain why three is subtracted from both sides. If your only reason is that the chatbot said so, return to the meaning of equality.
shots.purpose: A small check before moving on

shots.text: Step two. Hide the answer. Close the screen. Take a fresh sheet, and explain the method from memory.
shots.caption: Step two. Hide the answer.
shots.purpose: Second numbered medallion; a large gloved hand shuts the computer.

shots.text: Ada subtracts three from both sides. Then she divides both sides by two. The number is four. Each step has a reason.
shots.caption: Explain why each step works.
shots.purpose: An overhead page reveals the reasoning one step at a time.

shots.title: A missing step tells you where to look
shots.caption: Use the smallest useful piece of help.
shots.text: Suppose Ada cannot explain the division. She can reopen that step, study its reason, and retry. She need not replace her entire attempt with a copied solution.
shots.purpose: A missing step tells you where to look

shots.title: A mistake worth finding
shots.caption: Check the operation, not just the final number.
shots.text: If she subtracts three on the left but forgets the right, the work can still look orderly. Substituting her proposed answer into the original equation exposes the mistake.
shots.purpose: A mistake worth finding

shots.text: Check the work. Put four back into the original equation. Two times four, plus three, is eleven. If something fails, correct it.
shots.caption: Check. Correct. Try again.
shots.purpose: Ada substitutes the result into the original equation and stamps a check.

shots.title: Name the error, then retry
shots.caption: Repair the reason that produced the mistake.
shots.text: Useful feedback names the error: apply the same operation to both sides. Ada corrects that step and tries another equation. A green check tells her less.
shots.purpose: Name the error, then retry

shots.text: Step three. Change the problem. New numbers are a start. A new situation checks whether you can choose the method yourself.
shots.caption: Step three. Change the problem.
shots.purpose: Third numbered medallion; the algebra sheet becomes a shop problem.

shots.text: Two notebooks and a three dollar delivery fee cost fifteen dollars. What does one notebook cost? Ada has to build the equation before solving it.
shots.caption: Choose the method in a new situation.
shots.purpose: Two notebooks, a delivery tag and a receipt establish a real transfer example.

shots.title: Build the equation first
shots.caption: Name the unknown before calculating.
shots.text: Let the unknown name one notebook's price. Two identical notebooks cost twice that amount. Delivery is charged once, adding three dollars to the total.
shots.purpose: Build the equation first

shots.title: The same structure, a new story
shots.caption: Two notebook prices plus one fee equal fifteen.
shots.text: Remove the three dollar delivery fee from fifteen dollars. Twelve dollars remain for two notebooks. Divide by two. The price is six dollars per notebook. This calculation follows the same equation structure.
shots.purpose: The same structure, a new story

shots.title: Check against the situation
shots.caption: Does the answer account for every part of the cost?
shots.text: Two notebooks at six dollars cost twelve. Add the three dollar fee: fifteen. The check connects the calculation back to the situation in the question.
shots.purpose: Check against the situation

shots.title: A changed story may need a changed model
shots.caption: Do not apply the last procedure automatically.
shots.text: If delivery is charged for each notebook, the equation changes. Similar words can hide different relationships. Explain which costs repeat before choosing a calculation.
shots.purpose: A changed story may need a changed model

shots.text: Come back later for another fresh problem, without the tool. That checks retention separately from what feels easy right now.
shots.caption: Return later. Try without the tool.
shots.purpose: Calendar page turns; a clean question awaits Ada with the computer closed.

shots.title: Make the later check fresh
shots.caption: Use a new question without the worked solution beside it.
shots.text: Use a fresh question for the later attempt. Put the old solution away. Record what you can do independently, then decide what to revisit.
shots.purpose: Make the later check fresh

shots.title: Compare prediction with performance
shots.caption: Let evidence update your confidence.
shots.text: Before checking, predict what you can explain. Compare that prediction with your actual work. Use the gap to choose your next practice, rather than relying on ease.
shots.purpose: Compare prediction with performance

shots.title: Use the same idea when writing
shots.caption: Choose the writing skill you want to practise.
shots.text: For writing, a chatbot's rewrite may improve the document. To practise argument, Ada can first state her own claim and the evidence she thinks supports it.
shots.purpose: Use the same idea when writing

shots.title: Ask for a reader’s question
shots.caption: Locate the weakness before accepting a rewrite.
shots.text: Ask which sentence is unsupported, or what a skeptical reader would question. Then revise the paragraph yourself and explain the change. Keep that decision with the writer.
shots.purpose: Ask for a reader’s question

shots.title: Try another paragraph
shots.caption: A polished draft is useful; a new attempt tests the skill.
shots.text: Later, write another paragraph without those suggestions. This adapts the routine to writing; it is not evidence that these exact prompts have been experimentally validated.
shots.purpose: Try another paragraph

shots.title: For code, predict before running
shots.caption: Explain what the program will do.
shots.text: For programming, explain what each line changes. Predict the result for a specific input, then run the function. Compare the execution with your prediction.
shots.purpose: For code, predict before running

shots.title: A passing example is only one case
shots.caption: Test the boundary your explanation depends on.
shots.text: This function returns the first item in a list. It works for a nonempty list. What happens with an empty one? Test the assumption behind that first success.
shots.purpose: A passing example is only one case

shots.title: Make and explain the repair
shots.caption: A new requirement creates another independent attempt.
shots.text: She adds an explicit check for an empty list. She explains what each branch returns. Then she tests a new requirement on her own, instead of simply accepting a patch.
shots.purpose: Make and explain the repair

shots.title: The tool’s explanation also needs checking
shots.caption: Use the relevant source, calculation or test.
shots.text: A clear explanation can be wrong. Check equations by substitution, code with suitable tests, and factual claims against reliable sources. The system's confidence is not independent verification.
shots.purpose: The tool’s explanation also needs checking
shots.aside: Confidence is not a verification method

shots.title: Support can remove the wrong obstacle
shots.caption: Keep the target skill clear.
shots.text: Language or accessibility support can free attention for the target skill. Practise that skill independently where appropriate; do not demand that every useful support disappear.
shots.purpose: Support can remove the wrong obstacle

shots.title: Sometimes the goal is the finished product
shots.caption: Decide what you need from this session.
shots.text: Sometimes a finished product is the goal. That is a different choice. Decide what to delegate, what to verify, and which capability you want to retain.
shots.purpose: Sometimes the goal is the finished product

shots.title: Turn the idea into one small session
shots.caption: Choose a skill, a question and a later check.
shots.text: Choose one skill to retain. Pick a suitable question and the help needed to begin. Reserve a fresh question for a later independent attempt.
shots.purpose: Turn the idea into one small session

shots.text: Attempt with suitable guidance. Hide, explain, and check. Change the problem, then return later. Keep the next independent attempt in view.
shots.caption: Attempt. Explain. Check. Transfer. Return.
shots.purpose: Pull back from the detail into the three-step manual card.

shots.title: Keep a useful practice record
shots.caption: Record the help, the gap and the next attempt.
shots.text: Record your attempt, the help used, the error corrected, and what you could do later. Look for progress in your own work, not the number of chatbot messages.
shots.purpose: Keep a useful practice record

shots.text: This is a practical check, not a universally proven recipe. The right amount of help depends on the learner and the task.
shots.caption: Match the help to the learner and the task.
shots.purpose: Tip ribbon makes the practical limits explicit.

shots.text: A finished page is useful. A skill you can use again is something more. What can you do when the answer is gone?
shots.caption: What can you do when the answer is gone?
shots.purpose: Return to Ada and a new successful page, then close into a circular end card.
Circular end title and source attribution.
